does: Draws water out of a watery vegetable with salt before it is cooked or dressed, so that it keeps its bite and does not flood the dish.
how: Slice or dice the vegetable and toss it with fine salt.
Leave it in a colander over a bowl until it has given up its water.
Rinse off the salt if the dish will be salted again, and press or pat the pieces dry.

cues.text: Liquid has collected under the colander, and the pieces have gone limp and glossy.

mistakes.mistake: Skipping the drying, so that the vegetable goes into the pan or the dressing still wet.
mistakes.fix: Press it gently in a cloth before you use it.

mistakes.mistake: Salting the dish as usual afterwards, so that it ends up far too salty.
mistakes.fix: Taste before you add any more salt.
